target_customer: Consumers and event organizers who need to share photos among large groups
problem: Sharing photos from events with many people is clumsy because of email limits and per-person accounts.
business_model: Free consumer web service; rooms lasted longer when invited friends joined (viral growth), no revenue model found

founders.name: Jonathan Berger
founders.background_notes: YC page lists product roles at Stripe, Box and Google and calls him a two-time founder; those roles may postdate Picurio, so not recorded as prior employers.

founders.name: Michael Kodiak
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background given

founders.name: Laura Savidge
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background given

competitors.name: Divvyshot
competitors.what: Group event photo sharing, also YC Winter 2009

technical_complexity.rationale: Web uploads, rooms with invitations, Facebook import and publish, zip downloads and an iPhoto-like interface per the July 2009 TechCrunch write-up; standard engineering for two people.

defensibility.rationale: Features described were copyable by Flickr, Photobucket, Facebook and Divvyshot; no data or network lock-in beyond temporary rooms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook photo albums with tagging already served group photos; Facebook bought rival Divvyshot in April 2010 per The Next Web. No source shows what happened to Picurio.

market_need_then: Event photo collection from many guests was a known pain point in 2009; TechCrunch pitched it as useful for large events where attendees need a central, optionally private place.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches for name origin, logo, mascot, rebrands and press about the brand returned nothing about this company, so the brand is rated at the floor on absence of evidence only. Name resembles other photo names such as Picvario and Picturio that appear in search results.

outcome_analysis: Picurio launched out of beta in July 2009 into a crowded photo sharing space where Facebook, Flickr and Photobucket already served groups. No funding beyond the YC deal, no exit and no shutdown reason were found, so the cause of inactivity is not public. The failure factors reflect the strong incumbents and a late entry, not a documented post-mortem.
notes: Website picurio.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch. Failure factors are inferred from competition, not stated by any source; shutdown cause is not public. Funding searches returned only unrelated companies (Picvario). YC page lists 3 founders but team size 2.
